title: Modern Decoder Building Blocks
description: Study rmsnorm and residual pathways, rotary positional embeddings, swiglu and feed-forward capacity, and grouped-query and multi-query attention. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: RMSNorm and residual pathways
lessons.description: Draw a pre-normalized decoder block and identify the residual path and normalization sites.
lessons.conceptOverview: RMSNorm rescales activations using their root mean square rather than subtracting a feature mean as LayerNorm does. Residual pathways preserve an additive route through a block. Placement and numerical precision affect optimization, so normalization is an architectural choice rather than a cosmetic replacement.
lessons.whyItMatters: RMSNorm and LayerNorm use different normalization statistics.

lessons.title: Rotary positional embeddings
lessons.description: Explain why rotating both queries and keys can make their interaction depend on relative position.
lessons.conceptOverview: RoPE applies position-dependent rotations to query and key components. Their dot products then encode relative positional relationships. Extending context through scaling changes how positions are represented and needs evaluation beyond simply changing a maximum-length setting.
lessons.whyItMatters: Context-extension changes require long-context quality evaluation.

lessons.title: SwiGLU and feed-forward capacity
lessons.description: Sketch the two branches, elementwise product, and output projection of a gated feed-forward block.
lessons.conceptOverview: A gated feed-forward block multiplies one transformed branch by a nonlinear gate from another branch. SwiGLU uses a swish-style activation in the gating structure. Hidden widths determine parameter and compute budgets, so compare gated and ordinary blocks at an explicit budget.
lessons.whyItMatters: Compare feed-forward variants with their actual hidden widths and parameter budgets.

lessons.title: Grouped-query and multi-query attention
lessons.description: Compute how cache storage changes when KV heads fall from eight to two with all other dimensions fixed.
lessons.conceptOverview: MHA gives attention heads separate keys and values. MQA shares one key/value head; GQA shares them within groups. Reducing KV heads shrinks cache storage, but changing a trained architecture is not a free inference-only switch with guaranteed identical quality.
lessons.whyItMatters: KV-head sharing reduces cache size while introducing an architectural tradeoff.
